title: Build a one-page project home
capability: A coding agent turns a written brief into files that meet it
brief:
You are building a one-page project home for a small independent release.

Produce exactly three files in the current directory. Do not create anything else.

1. app.json
   {
     "title": string,
     "tagline": string,
     "theme": "light" or "dark",
     "links": [ { "label": string, "url": string } ],
     "sections": ["about", "guestbook"]
   }
   Use this title: "Night Shift Radio". Use this tagline: "Two hours of quiet, made on a kitchen table."
   Use exactly these three links, in this order, with these labels:
     "Latest release" -> https://example.com/release
     "Behind the scenes" -> https://example.com/notes
     "Get the newsletter" -> https://example.com/subscribe

2. app.css
   All styling lives here. The page itself must contain no inline style attributes and no <style> blocks.

3. index.html
   One complete page linking app.css. It must show the title and the tagline, list all three links with their exact labels, and give the about and guestbook sections a heading each.

Hard constraints, checked by a script:
- No <script> elements and no on* event handler attributes.
- No inline style attributes and no <style> blocks. The page is served under a Content-Security-Policy that blocks them.
- No requests to other origins. The only https URLs allowed are the three link targets above.
- One <h1> only. The page declares a language. Include the viewport meta tag.
- Every link has visible text.

Write the files, check them against the brief yourself, then stop.

assertions.name: app.json is a valid manifest with the required shape
The manifest carries the given title, tagline and three links in order
index.html shows the title, tagline and all three labels
index.html links app.css and app.css declares styling
No script, no inline style attributes and no style blocks
One h1, a declared language, a viewport meta and no empty links
The about and guestbook sections each have a heading
